title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 6th District
area: Piedmont Triad region, including High Point and Greensboro.

context.text: Incumbent Addison McDowell (R) advanced from a canceled Republican primary. Cyril Jefferson won a contested Democratic primary. Independent Joshua Hager did not make the general-election ballot. No Libertarian or other minor-party candidate is listed for this district.

candidates.name: Addison McDowell

summary.text: Addison McDowell is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 6th Congressional District. A former congressional staffer and Blue Cross Blue Shield lobbyist, he was first elected in 2024 and took office in January 2025 as one of the youngest members of Congress. His office says his top priorities are addressing the drug crisis and border security.

background.text: Born in 1994; Ballotpedia lists Whiteville, North Carolina as his birthplace, and his House biography describes him as a native of Lexington, North Carolina.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte.
In 2016, while he was in college, his younger brother Luke died after taking a pill laced with fentanyl; McDowell has said that loss motivated him to seek office.
Worked on staff for Reps. Richard Hudson and Ted Budd (now a U.S. Senator), helping constituents, according to his House biography.
Worked as a lobbyist for Blue Cross Blue Shield.

Won a crowded 2024 Republican primary for the open seat after endorsement by Donald Trump, then won the November 2024 general election; it was his first elected position. He succeeded Democrat Kathy Manning, who did not seek re-election after the district was redrawn.
Serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure, Natural Resources, and Budget committees. Advanced to the 2026 general election after the Republican primary was canceled.
Lives in Davie County with his wife, Rachel, and their two daughters, according to his House biography.

priorities.text: Tackling the drug crisis and strengthening border security, a priority he traces to his younger brother's death from a fentanyl overdose.

positions.summary: Says the right to self-defense is a constitutional right and he will fight government efforts he views as disrupting North Carolinians' Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: Addison believes that the right to self-defense is a God-given, constitutional right of every law-abiding American. As an avid hunter and gun enthusiast, Addison will fight government overreach that aims to disrupt North Carolinians' 2nd Amendment rights.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Indian and Insular Affairs; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees), the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation; Highways and Transit subcommittees), and the House Committee on Budget.

candidates.name: Cyril Jefferson
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested March 3, 2026 Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: Mayor of High Point, North Carolina

summary.text: Cyril Jefferson is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Addison McDowell in North Carolina's 6th Congressional District. He is the mayor of High Point, first elected to the city council in 2019 and as mayor in 2023, and the founder of a social-innovation consulting firm.

background.text: Attended North Carolina A&T State University and High Point University for undergraduate study; his campaign biography describes him as a graduate of North Carolina A&T.
Founder and principal of Change Often, a social innovation firm that says it has helped invest more than $22 million in initiatives for small-business support, poverty alleviation and education.

Has worked as an educator, education policy fellow, youth development consultant and motivational speaker, and has been affiliated with the United Way, the Chamber of Commerce, the Jaycees, the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative and the NAACP.
Elected to the High Point City Council Ward 1 seat in the 2019 nonpartisan election, defeating Willie Davis.

Elected Mayor of High Point in the 2023 city elections; his campaign biography says he is the youngest person elected to that office. Has received a National Distinguished Service Award and a Hunt State Policy Fellowship, according to his campaign biography.
Launched his campaign for Congress in August 2025 and won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Alysa Kassay, Keith Davenport and others.
According to his campaign biography, he is married to Raven and they have two sons.

priorities.text: Says his approach is to put people first, build strong partnerships, and focus on practical solutions rather than political rhetoric.

positions.summary: In a WSOC-TV candidate questionnaire, said he would protect Medicaid and Medicare and lower prescription drug costs.
positions.quote: It also means protecting healthcare programs like Medicaid and Medicare, lowering prescription drug costs, treating mental health like physical health, and addressing hunger as a health issue.

positions.summary: Says he does not support fear-based approaches to immigration but supports adding border agents, judges and E-Verify.
positions.quote: I do not support approaches to immigration that rely on fear, chaos, or the dehumanization of people.

positions.summary: In a WSOC-TV candidate questionnaire, said U.S. policy should ensure Israel's security while conditioning security assistance on adherence to humanitarian standards.
positions.quote: Security assistance should be conditioned on adherence to humanitarian standards, ensuring U.S. support does not contribute to disproportionate harm and that humanitarian access remains non-negotiable.

record.text: Serves as Mayor of High Point, North Carolina, since being elected in 2023.

candidates.researchNotes: Jefferson's 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey emphasizes his biography and leadership philosophy over specific policy stances; no detailed issue-by-issue positions were found within the research budget.
